blocks.task_summary: Find the smallest positive integer n such that z^n = −i for z = cos(11π/18) + i sin(11π/18).
method_path: Apply De Moivre's theorem: z^n = cos(11πn/18) + i sin(11πn/18)
Set z^n = −i and equate arguments: 11πn/18 = 3π/2 + 2kπ, k ∈ ℤ
Find least positive integer solution: k = 2 ⇒ n = 9
accepted_alternatives: Equate imaginary parts instead of arguments: sin(11πn/18) = −1 along with cos(11πn/18) = 0

evidence.basis: attempt to use De Moivre's theorem (M1); attempt to consider imaginary part (M1) OR attempt to consider argument of −i (M1); 11πn/18 = 3π/2 + 2kπ or 110n = 270 + 360k (A1); n = 9 A1

blocks.task_summary: Describe a single geometric transformation applied to z on the Argand diagram that results in z^10.
method_path: Find angular difference: arg(z^10) − arg(z) = π/9 − 11π/18 = −π/2
State transformation: rotation about the origin by −π/2 (clockwise π/2, or 3π/2 counterclockwise)
accepted_alternatives: Recognise z^10 = z^9 × z and use z^9 = −i from part (a); multiplication by −i corresponds to rotation by 3π/2 (or −π/2) about the origin.

evidence.basis: EITHER arg(z^10) = 55π/9 = π/9 (A1); recognising that the difference between arg(z^10) and arg(z) is needed (M1); arg(z^10)−arg(z) = −π/2 OR recognising that z^10 = z^9 × z (M1); z^9 = e^{i·3π/2} (A1); THEN a rotation 3π/2 OR π/2 clockwise about the origin A1
